rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F = k q₁q₂/r²
E = F/q
∮E·dA = Q/ε₀

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Coulomb: F = (1/4πε₀)·q₁q₂/r². Electric field E = F/q = kq/r²; for a line/dipole use superposition.  ·  Gauss's law: ∮E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀ — powerful for spherical/cylindrical/planar symmetry.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Superposition principle.** The force on any one charge due to several others equals the vector sum of the individual pairwise forces, each calculated as if the rest were absent.  ·  **Method.** Draw each Coulomb force on the chosen charge, resolve into components along convenient axes, sum the components, then combine for the net force.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Potential V = kq/r; ΔV = W/q; U of a charge in potential = qV. Equipotential surfaces are ⟂ to field lines.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Collinear charges.** For three charges on a line the middle charge feels opposing forces; the net force points toward the weaker side and vanishes only in a carefully balanced position.  ·  **Link to electric field.** The net force can be written F = qE, where E is the total field produced at the charge's position by all the other charges.  ·  **System energy.** The potential energy of a charge system is the sum of the pairwise terms kqᵢqⱼ/rᵢⱼ — counted once per pair, never twice.
